sites.name: Chang'e-7 planned landing site (peak near SE ridge of Shackleton)
sites.notes: verified: Wikipedia states the coordinate, but its only citation is a 2023 Weibo post (ref [4]). Its other landing-site reference, SpaceNews (Jan 2024), only says 'Shackleton'. The Planetary Society, Gunter's Space Page, a 2023 ThePaper interview with chief designer Wu Weiren ('several candidate sites identified') and a 2026 ITHome article ('south of 85°S') give no coordinates. The NSR payload paper (PMC10880881) could not be fetched because of a CAPTCHA; per the prior researcher and the Planetary Society it shows only a map. No official CNSA coordinate was found. The longitude is east. Sanity checks: the cached LOLA DEM shows this point (about 1632 m) within about 20 m of a local high (1647.5 m at -88.81, 123.71), which is consistent with a 'peak'. By calculation, using the IAU Shackleton center (-89.67, 129.78; D = 21 km), the point lies about 26 km from Shackleton's center, so roughly 15 km outside the rim rather than on it. Treat this as an approximate, unofficial candidate at 0.1° precision. Status: rolled out on Long March 5 Y14 on 19 Aug 2026; the launch was scrubbed about 23-24 Aug 2026 (Tropical Storm/Typhoon Narra and readiness) and delayed to 2027.

The site is an intercrater area within about 1.5 km of its target near the crater Malapert A. NASA asked for this site to learn how to send data to Earth from a spot low on the lunar horizon. The coordinate, 89.45 S, 137.15 W (given as 222.85 E), comes from a 2025 newsletter by Jatan Mehta reporting a 2024 IAC talk by Veeramuthuvel of ISRO, who said the landing site could be there; it is secondhand and hedged, not a confirmed target.
